## Per-issue source notes

These notes retain all linked PR summaries and all explicit remaining-scope lines. Earlier limits can be superseded by later PRs. Absence of a later reference does not prove that a limit was fixed.

### Issue 1

Milestone in PR #381: M1. Current GitHub state: open.

Original acceptance scope at collection:

Decide how `spinal-boom` uses the workstation. Requirement: EDA development and BOOM development run in parallel, and BOOM can pull tool changes when it wants them. Breaking changes are allowed when the docs describe them.

Proposed model: BOOM pins a workstation version (tag or commit) and upgrades with one command; BOOM owns its glue; each release has a changelog with upgrade steps; each side tests against a pinned version of the other.

Tasks after the decision:
- [ ] Move BOOM's project files (`rvw.toml`, adapter, suites, waivers, cosim and debug config, SpinalDB/SpinalChecks entries) into `spinal-boom`. A tested copy is on branch `rvw-project` of the private clone.
- [ ] Add the `rvw` workflow to the core agent's instructions.
- [ ] Choose and tune BOOM's gem5 model (queue model, event counters, fitting) in BOOM's project files.

## Additional scope

- [ ] Keep BOOM adoption separate from the generic distribution decision in #34. Define core-owned migration tasks only after that decision.
- [ ] List Konata tracer hooks and duplicate ProbeRun code. Require old/new trace parity and explicit removal conditions before migration. Keep core changes in riscPrint/spinal-boom. Evidence: existing #1; `SpinalKonata/README.md:93-100`; `ROADMAP.md:40-55`.

### Issue 5

Milestone in PR #381: M2. Current GitHub state: open.

Original acceptance scope at collection:

516 checks, 484 inserted, 32 waived; 24 `stream.valid_hold` / `stream.payload_stable` checks fire. Likely cause: BOOM comes from Chisel, whose `Decoupled` lets `valid` drop before `ready`.
- [x] Add a per-stream "may drop valid" setting.
- [ ] Decide each firing: legal drop (with reason) or core bug (report in TODO for `spinal-boom`).

## Additional scope

- [ ] Link all 24 stream IDs to a reasoned disposition and riscPrint/spinal-boom#7. Keep legal Decoupled valid drops separate from confirmed core defects. Evidence: existing #5; `SpinalChecks/README.md:245-247`.

Gray recognition accepts both Spinal shift forms and a register that copies a Gray wire. `cdc.hierarchy` groups findings by component. - Functional CDC step: `rvw lint --emit DIR` writes `rvw.cdc-obligations/1`, `cdc_checks.sv` (checker modules `rvw_cdc_gray`, `rvw_cdc_stable` and `bind` lines) and `checked/` RTL copies with the checkers inside the target modules (Yosys does not elaborate `bind`). - `rvw/src/rvw/lint/rules.py`: new `rules` backend with 15 design-database rules (combinational loops, multiple drivers, driven inputs, latches, width truncation/extension, unused, unconnected outputs, undriven, constant registers, unreachable FSM states, no reset, clock as data, naming, max fan-out), configurable severities and parameters, exact-ID waivers. - `rvw lint --sarif PATH`: SARIF 2.1.0 of all findings, with fingerprints and waiver suppressions. - New extracted reference `SpinalDB/.../LintLibraryFixtures.scala` (BufferCC, StreamFifoCC, PulseCCByToggle, ResetCtrl reset synchronizer, divided clock). - Shared format: additive `rvw.lint/1` fields and the new `rvw.cdc-obligations/1`, documented in `docs/PLATFORM_CONTRACTS.md`. No SpinalDB schema change.
  Evidence: ran on seeded RTL fixture.
  Explicit limits: Not run: BOOM or VexRiscv databases, `rvw formal bmc&#124;prove` on emitted checks, simulation of `cdc_checks.sv`, full Python suite. Refs: #22. Remains: the checkers are single-clock immediate assertions with level semantics (toggle protocols need their own monitor); a structural match is still not a protocol proof; no frequency data; non-Spinal domain import; commercial comparison.

- [#471](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/471): - New `SpinalChecks/src/main/scala/spinalchecks/CdcChecks.scala`: `CdcChecks.install(config)` adds an elaboration phase before `PhaseInsertChecks`. It finds every register with Spinal's `crossClockDomain` tag whose data comes, through plain copies, from a register in another clock, and declares: - `cdc.gray`: a multi-bit source changes at most one bit per source clock; - `cdc.pulse_width`: a one-bit source holds each value for `ceil(settle * f_src / f_dst)` source cycles, when both domains have a Spinal `FixedFrequency`. The checks are `DeclaredRule`s, so ids, waivers, Assert/Monitor modes and the report work as for other SpinalChecks rules. - `rvw lint` reads Spinal `setSynchronousWith` (`ClockSyncTag` signal tags) as a `declared_synchronous` clock relationship. - Docs: SpinalChecks README section and the lint README.
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Not run: full SpinalChecks sbt suite, formal runs of the new checks, BOOM. Refs: #22. Remains: sampled digital checks only (no metastability, setup/hold or phase model); handshake/toggle data-stability checks inside Spinal are not added yet.

- [#486](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/486): - `rvw query build-hdl` (`rvw/src/rvw/query/hdl.py`) now writes `clock_domains` from Yosys flip-flop cells: clock and reset nets followed through ports to toplevel inputs, `clock_edge` from `CLK_POLARITY`, `ASYNC` for `$adff`/`$adffe`/`$adlatch`, `SYNC` for `$sdff*`, polarity and `reset_value`. Registers get `clock_domain_id`; roots get `clock_role`. - Clock and reset pins are no longer data edges (the same as Spinal databases). Hidden Yosys temporaries become aliases of the one visible name of a bit; only visible names become registers. - `rvw lint`: the shared graph view drops hidden alias pairs for `yosys-verilog` databases, and `structural.py` uses that view (one edge map for CDC, RDC and depth checks). CDC/RDC classes now work on non-Spinal Verilog. - Shared format: no new tables or columns. `build-hdl` databases fill existing columns (`clock_domains`, `signals.clock_domain_id`, `reset_value`, `clock_role`) and drop clock/reset `sel` edges. Documented in `SpinalDB/README.md`.
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Not run: large Verilog designs, the full Python suite. Refs: #22 (non-Spinal domain import). Remains: synchronous resets in plain mux logic stay data; no memories or blackboxes in the HDL importer.

- [#528](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/528): Running `rvw query build-hdl` + `rvw lint` (rules, structural, sdc) on the SERV core (`ref/serv`, `serv_top`, 219 registers) showed false findings from Verilog imports. This fixes them:
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Not run: other cores, the full Python suite. Refs: #22. Remains: synchronous resets in plain mux logic are data in the HDL import; a loop across bits of one merged register vector cannot occur, but cross-bit wire loops through shared names are found only at bit level.

- [#540](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/540): - New VS Code feature `vscode/features/lint/`: **Lint: Run rvw lint** (settings from `lint.settings` or a file picker), **Run Again**, **Open Saved Report or SARIF**, **Clear Diagnostics**. - Findings from every backend (native lint, `rules`, `structural` CDC/RDC, `sdc`) become diagnostics in the Problems panel at their file and line; RTL `file:line:col` endpoints are parsed; unlocated findings go to line 1 of the settings file. Rule ID as code, `rvw lint &lt;backend>` as source. Waived findings are hints with their reason; stale waivers are errors. - Status bar: report status, active/waived counts and backends not run. It shows the report status as written; it never says clean unless `rvw lint` did. - Parsing is in `src/model.ts` (no VS Code API) with unit tests for rvw.lint/1, SARIF 2.1.0, errors and inconclusive reports.
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Status bar: report status, active/waived counts and backends not run. It shows the report status as written; it never says clean unless `rvw lint` did. Not run: the extension in a real VS Code window (no integration test for this feature), `npm run package`. Refs: #22 (editor output). Remains: no quick fixes or waiver editing in the editor.

- [#548](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/548): - CDC: qualified data whose qualifier source register toggles itself is a toggle handshake (`StreamCCByToggle` shape). It gets a `toggle_stable` obligation, and `rvw lint --emit` writes checker `rvw_cdc_toggle`: data changes only in the cycle the request toggles. `rvw.cdc-obligations/1` gains the kind (documented). - VS Code lint feature: quick fix **Copy rvw lint waiver for &lt;rule>** copies an exact waiver row (config, rule, endpoint, `finding_id`) with a `TODO` reason; stale-waiver and id-less findings are refused. Diagnostics now keep the finding id (from rvw.lint/1 or the SARIF fingerprint).
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Not run: the extension in a real VS Code window.

### Issue 34

Milestone in PR #381: M1. Current GitHub state: open.

Original acceptance scope at collection:

Decide how existing core designs adopt the workstation. The choice drives packaging and distribution. BOOM is the first user (#1). Owner requirements: the workstation and the core develop in parallel; a core pulls tool changes when it chooses; breaking changes are allowed when docs describe them; no submodules; native tools, no Docker.

## The parts and how each could ship

| Part | Proposed distribution | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|
| `rvw` (Python: CLI, MCP, gate, cosim, query) | PyPI package: `uv tool install rvw` (or a pinned git tag) | git clone + `scripts/install.sh` (today) |
| Scala libraries (RiscvSim, SpinalDB, SpinalChecks, SpinalKonata) | Maven artifacts (GitHub Packages, later Maven Central): `"io.riscprint" %% "riscvsim" % "0.1.0"` in the core's `build.sbt` | sbt source dependency on `RVW_HOME` (today); `publishLocal` |
| Native tools (Verilator, Yosys, Spike, gem5, Spike shim) | `rvw doctor --install` (the `install.sh` logic inside `rvw`): Homebrew / apt / dnf | `scripts/install.sh` (today); later a pinned tool bundle per OS |
| VS Code extension | VS Code Marketplace / Open VSX | `.vsix` from releases |

## Integration points

1. **`rvw init`** in the core repo scaffolds `rvw.toml`, the `rvw/` folder, the adapter skeleton, the sbt dependency and a version pin (#36).
2. **Agent playbook** in the core repo (an `AGENTS.md` section or skill written by `rvw init`) so an agent finishes the adapter and the first gate.
3. **Version pin and upgrade:** `rvw.toml` declares `requires = "rvw ~= 0.1"`; `rvw` refuses a version outside the range; `rvw upgrade` moves the pin and prints the changelog's upgrade steps. One version number for the Python package and the Scala libraries.
4. **CI:** a GitHub Action (`riscprint/rvw-action`) runs the gate on each pull request and posts the headline (TESTS PASS / NOT ACCEPTED, ACCEPT, REJECT) as a check.

## User journey (proposed)

```sh
uv tool install rvw
rvw doctor --install sim,cosim
cd my-core && rvw init
# an agent finishes the adapter with the playbook
rvw regress gate
```

## Options considered

- **A. Installed tool + project file + packages (recommended):** the table above. Standard for each ecosystem; parallel development through version pins.
- **B. Installed tool + project file, git-only:** clone at a tag + `install.sh`; Scala libraries as source dependencies through `RVW_HOME`. No package publishing, but every user builds the Scala libraries.
- **C. sbt plugin (`addSbtPlugin("io.riscprint" % "sbt-rvw")`):** natural for Spinal users; makes non-Spinal cores depend on sbt. Possible later as a convenience on top of A.
- **D. Vendoring (copy into the core) / submodules:** ruled out by the owner.

## Decision needed
- [ ] Choose the model (A, B, C or a mix).
- [ ] Package names and registry (PyPI name, Maven group ID, GitHub Packages or Maven Central).
- [ ] Versioning policy (semver from 0.x; which changes need upgrade steps).

## Additional scope

- [ ] Validate project and artifact schemas against the selected tool version before work starts.
- [ ] Add dry-run migration checks and explicit unsupported-format errors. Do not silently reinterpret evidence from older contracts. Evidence: `docs/PLATFORM_CONTRACTS.md:232-460,683-844`; `docs/BRING_YOUR_OWN_CORE.md:228-327`; `docs/BRING_YOUR_OWN_CORE.md:14-97,100-204,329-450`; `docs/AGENT_SETUP.md:1-65`; `AGENTS.md`, Working rules. Related: #34, #15, #35, #36.

- [x] Keep the owner decision open. Project selection already exists. Do not treat proposed packaging as approved.
- [x] Replace the #init issue placeholder with #36 when issue editing is authorized. Record distribution, package version and upgrade-policy decisions without selecting them in this audit. Evidence: existing #34; `ROADMAP.md:40-55`.

- [#556](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/556): - New tool `rvw fault` (`rvw/src/rvw/fault/`, README, Layout row) with these subcommands: - `sites`: register sites from the design database (`signals`, kind `reg`, not pruned; generated registers only on request; include/exclude globs). - `plan`: a seeded sample of `stuck0`, `stuck1` and `flip` faults over a cycle window. It records the population (site bits × cycles × kinds) and uses exhaustive mode when the population is small. - `run`: a golden run plus one run per fault through the core adapter (`run --fault FILE`, new optional C1 extension). The adapter must confirm the injection in `details.fault`, so injection success is measured separately from detection. Each fault is classified against the golden C2 architectural records: `detected` (failure status, a declared mechanism in `details.detections`, or a timeout with `--watchdog`), `silent_corruption`, `safe`, `timeout`, `not_injected` or `inconclusive`. - `report`: counts, denominators, sampled fraction, diagnostic coverage with a 95 % Wilson interval, safe fraction, unresolved faults. Outputs also include C3 (`fault-campaign`: detected or safe = pass, SDC = fail) and `outcomes.json` with the evidence for each fault. There is no ISO 26262 or reliability claim. - MCP: `fault_sites`, `fault_run`, `fault_report`. Contract: "C1 fault injection".
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Not run: no real core adapter implements `--fault` yet. The RiscvSim BOOM adapter does not.

- [#689](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/689): - Generic `run --fault FILE` (C1 fault injection) in `RiscvSim/src` for any adapter that runs through `SimSession`; no adapter code and no core names. - Fault jobs use a separate `_fault` model: an elaboration phase tags every register `simPublic`, and Verilator gets `--public-flat-rw` so outside writes re-evaluate readers. Golden runs keep the normal model. - The injector resolves `site` as the design-database register path, writes the bit after each clock edge in the window (`stuck0`/`stuck1` for `duration` or to the end, `flip` once), and confirms by reading the register back one time unit later. `details.fault` adds `applied_cycle`, `before`, `after`, `writes`. Missing sites, enumeration registers, out-of-range bits, runs that end first and failed read-backs give `applied: false` with a reason. Replay commands carry `--fault`. - Docs: `docs/contracts/c2-rvfi-trace.md` ("RiscvSim harness hooks"), `RiscvSim/README.md` ("Fault injection"), fault README.

Proposed shape:
- [ ] **Job image:** one image per tool set (Verilator, Spike, Yosys/SymbiYosys, gem5), built from the tested tool-version table (#40). Containers are execution hosts on the cluster only; the local workstation stays native.
- [ ] **Executor:** an `rvw` executor backend (`--executor k8s`) next to the local one. `rvw regress run`/`gate` split work into job shards (one manifest per pod, like `run-many`), submit them as an indexed Job, and collect C1 results.
- [ ] **Build once, run many:** build the Verilator model once per `rtl_sha256` + options, store it, and let all shards reuse it (with #14 and #53).
- [ ] **Inputs and results:** inputs follow C8 (ELFs, model and tools identified by hash); results go to object storage or a shared volume and are published as one generation. Shard failures and pod evictions give `inconclusive`, never a pass.
- [ ] **Limits:** CPU/memory requests per job type, concurrency caps, timeouts, and run budgets (#57).
- [ ] **Observability:** progress, logs and per-shard status through `rvw` and MCP background jobs.
- [ ] **Scale test:** full ACT4 + riscv-tests + benchmarks over many seeds on BOOM, compared against a local run of the same commit (same verdict).

Related: #14 (persistent sim server), #25 (regression farm), #53 (remote result cache), #57 (budgets).

- [#473](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/473): - `rvw debug interop`: GDB starts OpenOCD over a pipe (`gdb_port pipe`) against a remote_bitbang target. The target is a running simulation (`--port`), or the reference model that `rvw debug serve` serves for a profile (`--profile`). - A GDB Python script checks each operation by its effect: `load` (the entry word equals the ELF bytes), register and memory writes (read back after the caches are flushed), software and hardware breakpoints (stop pc and loop counter), `stepi` and the jump step, a watchpoint (counter advanced, pc after the store), and `monitor reset halt` (pc equals the declared reset pc). - C3 results (`debug-interop`) record the GDB and OpenOCD versions in `clients`. A connection without these effects is not a pass. A GDB error belongs to the first check it did not reach. Unreached checks are inconclusive. - Fixture `rvw/tests/fixtures/debug/interop.S`. MCP tool `debug_interop`.
  Evidence: reference model only (Spike/Sail/Python).
  Explicit limits: Not run: no core RTL target.

- [ ] Add identity-bound waveform indexing and range queries for large traces with measured memory limits.
- [x] Reuse native FST or an existing indexed reader where possible. Keep cut validity and unknown bits intact.
Evidence: `rvw/src/rvw/bundle/README.md:24-71,101-108`; `rvw/src/rvw/wave/README.md:1-71`; `vscode/README.md:3-7`; `ROADMAP.md:128-137`.
Related: #24, #43, #69.

- [#412](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/412): - `rvw wave find WAVE EXPR`: first time, last interval and all intervals where an expression over several signals holds (`&& &#124;&#124; !`, comparisons, arithmetic, bit selects, `rose/fell/changed/stable/known`). x/z use three-valued logic; an unknown result never counts as true and is counted in `unknown_steps`. - `rvw wave edges WAVE REGEX`: value changes, rising/falling edges (1-bit) and x/z transitions per signal in a window. - Both read only the referenced signals' rows from a `.rvwi` index (merged per-signal `signal_time` cursors); on VCD/FST they stream one pass. - `rvw wave index --reader wellen`: reads FST natively through pywellen (wellen, Surfer's reader), one signal at a time, with no `fst2vcd` conversion. `auto` (default) selects it for FST when the new `waves` extra is installed. - `--indexed` on every wave query (MCP `indexed`): a cached index per absolute wave path under `RVW_WAVE_INDEX_DIR`, rebuilt when the wave's recorded size/mtime differs. `rvw wave verify INDEX` compares full SHA-256 (exit 1 when stale). The build fails if the source changes while it is indexed. - MCP: `wave_find`, `wave_edges`, `wave_index`, `wave_index_verify`. - Fix: MCP wave tools on `.rvwi` input failed (`module 'rvw.wave.ops' has no attribute '_sample'`). The new MCP test fails without the `capture.py` fix. - PLATFORM_CONTRACTS: optional `source_stat`/`reader` metadata, wellen row order, cache layout.
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Not run: multi-GB FST, full Python suite, Linux. Refs: #173. Direct native FST reading now works for index builds. Remaining: wellen still loads one signal fully into memory (a single huge signal is not bounded), and SQLite insertion dominates build time.

- [#529](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/529): - `rvw wave find&#124;edges&#124;seq&#124;txn&#124;diff` on `.fst` read the wave directly through wellen (pywellen, `waves` extra): only the referenced signals are decoded, with a bisect to the window start; no `fst2vcd` conversion and no index needed. `RVW_WAVE_FST_READER=vcd` keeps the converter path; without pywellen nothing changes. - Shared `wellen_header` helper for the index builder and the direct reader. - Limit (documented): pywellen does not expose the FST end time, so an interval still open at the end uses the last change of the signals read for `true_time`.
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Not run: multi-GB FST. Refs: #173. Direct native FST seeking now covers the search commands. Remaining: `changes`/`sample`/`cut` on FST still use the converter (or an index), and a single huge signal is decoded whole by wellen.

- [#566](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/566): Fix for the direct FST reader from #529 and the wellen index reader from #412:
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: None stated. Owner review is required.

- [#541](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/541): - `ntrace.py`: a separate, versioned N-Trace codec `rvw-ntrace/1`. It has a reference encoder from C2 (BTM and HTM modes, periodic sync, history and ICNT overflow through ResourceFull, Ownership on privilege change, traps as BTYPE 1), MDO/MSEO byte packing and unpacking, and a decoder that follows the ELF program image. E-Trace support never counts as N-Trace support. - `rvw debug ntrace-check`: builds the expected stream from C2 (one encode per qualified window when `--filter` is set) and compares captured messages. It decodes in windows split at Error messages, known gaps and decode failures, and resyncs only at ProgTraceSync. Verdicts: `flow_match`, `partial_match`, `mismatch`, `leak`. A capture without its stop message is not a full match. - `rvw debug ntrace-loss`: drop, overflow (Error), wrap and truncate faults with C3 results (`ntrace-loss`). - Vendor adapters (`rvw.trace-adapter/1`) and `rvw debug trace-adapter`: an adapter must cite a specification and a license and give known packet vectors that unpack and repack exactly. An adapter without vectors is refused, because a vendor name is not evidence. `examples/trace/nexus-htm-template.toml` is a template whose vectors come from the rvw codec. No SiFive or Andes adapter is bundled, because there are no license-cleared vendor vectors. - `Asm.auipc` for the model hart.
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Not run: no RTL N-Trace encoder capture; no vendor vectors.

- [#512](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/512): - E-Trace ingress (`etrace_flow.py`) now covers exceptions, interrupts, trap returns and privilege changes. Trap causes come from C2 trap events. An exception is an exception-only entry at the trapping pc. xRET is reported as itype 6, which is what the pinned baseline encoder and decoder need (see the README). - `rvw debug etrace-check`: builds the expected stream from C2 with the pinned reference encoder and compares a capture (`.te_inst` or `.te_inst_raw`) field by field. It decodes the capture in segments split at known gaps (`--loss-at`) and trace-lost support packets, resyncs only at sync-start packets, aligns each segment with C2 in order, and reports lost spans as `unknown` windows. It never shows guessed execution. `--filter` (privilege, address ranges, exclusions, start/stop) gives one reference encode per qualified window, and a `leak` verdict for decoded PCs or sync addresses from unqualified execution. - `rvw debug etrace-loss`: drop, overflow, wrap and truncate faults at sampled positions, with C3 results (`etrace-loss`). - Test helper `rvw/tests/spike_c2.py` (Spike commit log to C2). Fixture `traps.S` (branches, M-mode and U-mode ecalls, mret).

### Issue 282

Milestone in PR #381: M6. Current GitHub state: open.

Original acceptance scope at collection:

SPEC CPU2017 needs a paid licence. Choose a free workload set for performance work on RISC-V cores. Keep SPEC as an optional plug-in for users with a licence.

## Candidates
- CoreMark-PRO (EEMBC): integer and floating-point workloads, closest free match to SPEC style.
- Embench-IoT and Embench DSP: small and reproducible; quick IPC checks.
- LLVM test-suite (MultiSource): many real C/C++ programs.
- GAP Benchmark Suite and Ligra: graph workloads, irregular memory access.
- PolyBench: loop kernels for memory and vector studies.
- Real applications: SQLite speedtest1, zstd, lz4, xz, gzip, QuickJS, Lua, a small compiler build, Verilator.
- PARSEC and SPLASH-3: multicore, later.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A short comparison: licence, coverage of integer/FP/memory/branch behaviour, size, RISC-V build status, input sets.
- [ ] A chosen default set, pinned (source revision, compiler, flags, inputs, expected outputs).
- [ ] Builds for RV64GC bare metal and Linux user mode where needed; outputs checked against a reference run (Spike or QEMU).
- [ ] A plan for SimPoint-style sampling so long programs run on RTL.
- [ ] SPEC CPU2017 stays optional: the same flow accepts it when a user supplies a licensed copy.

Related: #12, #56, #183.

- [#501](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/501): Add pinned riscv-tests, CoreMark-derived smoke, and zstd recipes to `rvw workloads`. Keep Embench as the default. Capture pinned source dependencies and copied runtime files. Reuse the architecture benchmark Makefile. Add cancellable workload MCP tools.

### Issue 335

Milestone in PR #381: M4. Current GitHub state: open.

Original acceptance scope at collection:

## Problem
`rvw bisect` and gates against an older base revision must build every core revision they test with today's workstation. The BOOM simulation interface changed over time (for example, at `a1c9b87` `BoomSimTop` takes different arguments, and the `Disasm` and `KonataTracer` hooks do not exist). The current adapter does not compile against those revisions, so bisect and the cold gate correctly report `inconclusive` instead of a result. Seen in #45 (bisect on real history) and #73 (cold gate against an older revision).

## Proposed fix (owner to decide; not started)
1. **Version-aware adapters (workstation):** keep a small adapter for each era of a core's simulation interface. Select the adapter from the revision under test (for example, by an interface version marker in the core or by a revision range in project data). The run identity (C1/C8) records which adapter was used.
2. **Stable interface from now on (core-side rule):** the core keeps its simulation interface backward-compatible, or bumps an explicit interface version when it must change. Then bisect works across every later commit. This needs agreement with the core track (riscPrint/spinal-boom).

## Acceptance
- [ ] Bisect across a range that spans at least one interface change gives a conclusive result, or an explicit `unsupported revision` for revisions with no adapter.
- [ ] A gate against an older base revision builds both sides.
- [ ] Adapter selection is recorded in the run identity and tested.
- [ ] Core-side interface-stability rule agreed and documented (linked spinal-boom issue).

Related: #45, #73, #34.

- [#474](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/474): Select captured project simulation adapters by exact revision or a version marker. Negotiate API 1 before launch. Pin script interpreters through C8. Record version, API, revision and manifest/executable hashes in supplied source identity. Unsupported revisions return no simulation result and remain bisect skips.
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Select captured project simulation adapters by exact revision or a version marker. Negotiate API 1 before launch. Pin script interpreters through C8. Record version, API, revision and manifest/executable hashes in supplied source identity. Unsupported revisions return no simulation result and remain bisect skips. Roadmap notes: #335 gains captured historical adapter resolution in debug launches used by bisect. Projects must supply the manifest and adapters in each captured core revision. Gate integration, actual historical core adapters and core-side stability agreement remain open. #45 remains unqualified: no real core history was executed and no guilty commit is claimed. NOT RUN: real historical core bisect, historical gates, BOOM, full Python suite, GitHub CI.

- [#714](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/714): Allow a captured debug configuration to select core.adapter_versions from a project registry outside historical source trees. Capture that registry and its support files. Resolve its commands inside the captured directory. Preserve exact revision selection, fail closed on unsupported revisions, record manifest_scope in adapter identity and prevent registry state from leaking to another core configuration.
  Evidence: ran on real core RTL.
  Explicit limits: NOT RUN: full Python suite, BOOM history, historical regression gates, a non-adjacent search campaign or GitHub CI. Refs: #335, #45. - [#558](https://github.com/riscPrint/risc-v-workstation/pull/558): - `frontend.op_cache`: a trace-driven micro-op cache in the csim front-end model. Lines are keyed by aligned fetch window (`window_bytes`); a window takes `ceil(ops / ops_per_line)` lines of one set (LRU), more than `max_lines_per_window` is uncacheable. A group hits when all its lines are present: it skips the I-cache and legacy decode and delivers `op_width` ops per cycle after `latency`; each change between op-cache and legacy delivery costs `switch_penalty`. Context rows flush it (default). - Report: lookups, hit rate, op coverage, fills, uncacheable windows, mode switches, context flushes, storage (`op_bits` per op). Sweep metric `op_cache_coverage`. - This is the csim component model; the gem5 micro-op cache in #359 stays with the arch area.
  Evidence: unit tests only.
  Explicit limits: Not run: op cracking or fusion (one instruction = one op), full slow suite, CI not awaited.

A net derived by other logic is now its own root instead of an arbitrary input found through the logic. - A register net's `reset_value` is now the concatenation of its own bits' reset values (before, every net got the whole cell's value). - `scripts/build-ghdl-plugin.py` builds a pinned ghdl-yosys-plugin revision with the GHDL headers of the exact libghdl commit, outside the checkout.
